'''Saka Haphong''' ({{lang-bn|সাকা হাফং}}, {{lang-my|ဆကးအဖောင် တောင်}}) is a peak in [[Southeast Asia]] and [[South Asia]] which was discovered by A.K.M Shahidullah Kaiser Sazzad Hossain and many others. Situated in [[Bangladesh]] and [[Myanmar]] it is often considered the highest point of the country (Bangladesh), with an elevation of {{convert|1025|m|ft|0}}.<ref name=irri>{{cite report|url=http://www.irri.org/GRC/Biodiversity/Pdffiles/BGDpdf/bgd3.pdf|title=A Report On BRRI-IRRI Cooperative Collection of Wild Oryza Species In Bangladesh|first=Bao-Rong |last=Lu|at=General information of the areas visited and the collecting routes|publisher=[[International Rice Research Institute]]|date=October 1998|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060813132803/http://www.irri.org/GRC/Biodiversity/Pdf%20files/BGD%20pdf/bgd3.pdf|archive-date=2006-08-13}}</ref> Located on the Bangladesh–[[Myanmar]] border, it is situated between [[Thanchi Upazila|Thanchi]], [[Bandarban]], Bangladesh and the [[Chin State]] of Myanmar.

Saka Haphong was believed to be the highest peak of Bangladesh,<ref>{{cite book |last=Chowdhury |first=Masud Hasan |year=2012 |chapter=Physiography |chapter-url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Physiography |editor1-last=Islam |editor1-first=Sirajul |editor1-link=Sirajul Islam |editor2-last=Jamal |editor2-first=Ahmed A. |title=Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh |edition=Second |publisher=[[Asiatic Society of Bangladesh]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/bangladesh/ |title=Bangladesh |website=The World Factbook |publisher=CIA}}</ref> but recent calculations have shown the highest peak of Bangladesh to be [[Tazing Dong]], which is officially recognized as such.<ref name="peakbagger"/> In February 2006 a GPS reading of 1,185 metres was recorded on this summit by Nature And Adventure Club [[Ginge Fullen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gingefullen.com/peaksclimbed.htm |title=World peaks climbed |website=Ginge Fullen |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729022014/http://www.gingefullen.com/peaksclimbed.htm |archive-date=29 July 2014}}{{self-published source|date=November 2015}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=November 2015}} The location he recorded,  21°47′11″N 92°36′36″E / 21.78639°N 92.61°E, accurately matches the location given by Russian topographic mapping<ref>{{cite web |url=http://download.maps.vlasenko.net/smtm200/g-46-26.jpg/ |title=Relevant section of the Topographic Map |date=1965 |website=Топографическая карта Украины, России, Беларуси |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501175606/http://download.maps.vlasenko.net/smtm200/g-46-26.jpg |archive-date=1 May 2013}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=November 2015}} and [[SRTM]] data, although these sources show its height to be slightly lower, at 1,052 metres.<ref name=otm>{{cite opentopomap|Saka Haphong|21.788611|92.608611|2023-03-05}}</ref> Recently two trekking clubs counted the height of Saka Haphong as 3,488 and 3,461 feet respectively,<ref>{{cite news |date=28 February 2011 |title='Second highest hill' spotted by 4 youths |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/newDesign/news-details.php?nid=175791/ |newspaper=The Daily Star}}</ref> both of which exceeds the height of [[Keokradong]] which is 3,172 feet high.
